anomalies.observed: The anodes of the three status LEDs D26 (yellow), D29 (green) and D38 (green) are all on /NET0083, and that net has no other connection. It is not tied to +3V3, to any driver output, or to any other supply. The cathodes are driven through R81 and R76 from the CM4 Ethernet nLED and PI_nLED_Activity lines.
anomalies.expected: A status LED driven through a series resistor from an active-low CM4 output needs its anode on a 3.3 V rail. D12 (the other yellow LED) gets its anode from +3V3, so the same arrangement is expected here.
anomalies.impact: The three LEDs can never light, so the Ethernet and activity status indication is lost.

anomalies.observed: On both isolated CAN transceivers, the bus-side ground pins GND2 (pin 5) and the logic-side ground pins GND1 (pin 4) are on the same GND net. The M12 CAN connector ground pins are also on GND. No separate isolated ground net exists anywhere in the netlist.
anomalies.expected: The specification describes two isolated CAN buses. Isolation needs GND2 on a separate, isolated bus ground, distinct from the logic GND at GND1.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller ... through an isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: The galvanic isolation the design relies on is defeated. Ground loops and common-mode faults can pass between the logic and bus sides.

anomalies.observed: On the dual LED D45, the second-channel cathode pin K2 (pin 2) goes through R34 to /NET0102. The anode pin A2 (pin 4) is also on /NET0102, so that channel is shorted by its own connections. The part's description says cathodes are on pins 1 and 3, which conflicts with the pin naming used here.
anomalies.expected: Each LED channel needs its anode and cathode on different nets, with the cathode on the ground side of the current-limit resistor.
anomalies.impact: The second LED channel of D45 would not light, or the pin mapping is wrong.

parsed.summary: The netlist has three status LEDs (D26, D29, D38) whose anodes sit on a net with no supply or driver, so they cannot light. The isolated CAN transceivers also have their two ground domains tied together, which defeats the stated isolation. The second channel of dual LED D45 is also shorted by its own pin connections. The first finding is the most likely real fault.
parsed.design_review_note: Confidence is moderate. Several of these may be original design choices rather than injected faults.
